title: The Best That Heaven Could Bring
description: The Best That Heaven Could Bring in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the East (Paisley, in print by 1911), headed “Rejoice, rejoice,”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The best that heaven could bring First fruits, an of-fering free Was brought from far, when, by the star, The wise men came to Thee.

lines: The best that heaven could bring —
Was brought from far, when, by the star,
The wise men came to Thee.
As, with surprise, on humble guise
O Christ, the Lord, Incarnate Word!

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the East (by 1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the East; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
